sections.h2: Who lives in Addison, and what are the homes like?
sections.html:
Addison is a DuPage County village where most sales involve a suburban house or condo that must clear a short list of village steps before the deed can move. Census estimators counted 35,758 people on July 1, 2025, a hair above the 35,702 recorded in 2020, so the housing stock is stable and fully built out.

The village sits on Salt Creek, a tributary of the Des Plaines River, and covers roughly ten square miles. It was first called Dunkley's Grove and was incorporated in 1884. Most of the houses date from the stretch after 1960, when developers turned farmland into subdivisions and the population jumped from 6,741 in 1960 to 24,482 in 1970. Most sellers here are marketing a house from that postwar and later building era.

The economy leans on freight and distribution. Census figures show 2022 transportation and warehousing receipts of $508,509 thousand in Addison, far above the $112,946 thousand recorded for restaurants and lodging. The village describes its economy as logistics, manufacturing and food distribution close to the interstates and O'Hare.

  • Home value among owners, 2020 to 2024 survey: $341,300
  • Share of homes lived in by owners: 67.0%
  • Typical monthly gross rent: $1,245
  • Median household income: $90,431
  • Households: 12,832, with a mean commute of 25.6 minutes

sections.h2: Which village steps must be finished before an Addison sale can close?
sections.html:
Addison will not issue a real estate transfer stamp until the sewer, permit, water and paperwork items on the Community Development and Finance pages are cleared. The village page says the deed cannot be transferred before the stamp is issued, so a missed item can delay the closing date.

  • Sewer compliance: the certificate cannot be older than six months on closing day, and the village wants the inspection booked a fortnight early through Community Development at (630) 693-7530.
  • Permit release: confirms no open building permits or unpaid inspection fees. A release stays valid for two months only.
  • Water: the seller books a final meter reading, done 24 hours before closing, and pays the final bill by noon the business day before closing. The buyer pre-registers for the water and sewer account.
  • Paperwork: the seller's attorney sends the village a copy of the PTAX-203 or PTAX-203A and a copy of the drafted deed.

Condominiums skip the water account and the sewer or sump inspection. The only requirement for a condo is the permit release.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed or foreclosure transfer still need an Addison stamp?
sections.html:
Yes. The village issues a zero-dollar exempt stamp for quitclaim deeds, deeds into a trust, foreclosures and sheriff sales, and it still charges the $50 processing fee. A lost stamp has to be repurchased in full, so keep the original with the closing file.

The exempt stamp needs the same sewer inspection, permit release and final water bill as a sale. The village also asks for its own Certificate of Exemption form and a copy of the signed and notarized deed. When the owner name on the deed is changing, the new owner must open a water and sewer account with two forms of identification. When the name is not changing, the water balance simply has to be paid before the stamp is released.

Heirs deeding an inherited Addison house should plan on the same items, even though no sale tax is due. Starting the sewer appointment early is the best way to protect the closing date.

sections.h2: What rules apply to an Addison house that is rented out?
sections.html:
Every Addison dwelling that is not owner-occupied and charges rent needs an annual Residential Rental License. The license year runs May 1 to April 30, renewal notices go out by mail in March, and renewals are due by April 30.

The village counts more than 1,000 licensed rental properties and nearly 4,000 rental units, and it grades each property after an annual inspection. In a single-family house, condo or townhouse the inspector walks the interior. In a multi-family building the village inspects 20 percent of the units plus the common areas. Owners must also attend an 8-hour Crime Free Multi-Housing class within 90 days of getting a license.

Addison bans short-term rentals outright and classes them as a nuisance, which matters to a buyer planning to put the house on a booking site. A landlord selling a licensed rental can email Rentals@addison-il.org or call the Rental Housing Supervisor line at (630) 693-7544 to ask how an open license year is handled at closing.

sections.h2: How does DuPage County bill property tax on an Addison home?
sections.html:
DuPage County sends one bill with two installment coupons, and the tax covers the prior year. For 2025 taxes, bills went out on April 29, 2026, with payments due on the first of June and the first of September. The DuPage County Treasurer at 630-407-5900 can confirm the dates for the next cycle.

Addison spans Addison and Bloomingdale townships, so the township assessor named on the bill is the first contact for valuation questions. The treasurer's office says it does not set values. It also warns that a yellow box on the bill means a mortgage servicer is already paying, and a second payment would later have to be refunded.

  • The treasurer puts both the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000.
  • Preliminary county figures for the 2025 levy showed assessed value up 8.2%, the average tax rate down 4.37% and the overall bill up 3.83%.
  • Individual bills differ by parcel because each one falls in a different mix of school, park and fire districts.

Because the bill arrives a year behind, ask the title officer how the current year's tax and any unpaid installment will be settled between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: Can an Addison owner appeal an assessment before listing?
sections.html:
An owner can file with the DuPage County Board of Review, but only inside the 30-day window that opens when the township roll is published. Section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code sets the deadline at 30 calendar days after publication, and the county says talking with the township assessor does not extend it.

DuPage asks for three or more comparable properties, with recent sales as the strongest evidence. Assessed values rest on the three prior years of sales, so the 2025 value drew on sales from 2022 through 2024. Written decisions usually arrive the following March. An owner who disagrees can go on to the state Property Tax Appeal Board or to court. An appeal challenges the assessed value only, and the tax rate stays with the local taxing districts.

sections.h2: What state transfer tax and declaration apply to an Addison sale?
sections.html:
Under Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code the state levies 50 cents on every $500 block of value stated on the transfer declaration. When the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the basis.

The declaration is filed on Form PTAX-203 or through the Department of Revenue's free MyDec system. Addison also wants its own copy of that form before it releases the village stamp, so the seller's attorney should send it to the water billing email listed on the village page.

sections.h2: What do Addison buyers look at beyond the house itself?
sections.html:
Buyers usually compare the school pattern, the commute and the age of the home. Addison Trail High School and Indian Trail Junior High anchor the public school map, and the elementary schools include Ardmore, Wesley, Lake Park, Fullerton, Army Trail, Lincoln and Stone. St. Philip the Apostle offers private Catholic schooling from pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.

Pace buses on Routes 711 and 715 connect Addison with Wheaton and other points. The average commute is 25.6 minutes, and 93.0% of residents had not moved in the previous year, which points to long ownership.

Addison owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell to a buyer who accepts the house in its current condition. A cash buyer still needs the same sewer certificate, permit release and final water bill, so the village timetable applies on every route. Owners with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses often choose the as-is route because repairs would otherwise be negotiated after the buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book the Addison sewer inspection?
faqs.a: Call Community Development at (630) 693-7530 and set the appointment a minimum of two weeks ahead. The certificate it produces must carry a date within six months of closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the Addison real estate transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The buyer. The village page calls the purchase of the stamp the buyer's responsibility and prints the standard rate as $2.50 for each $1,000 of purchase price.

faqs.q: Do condos in Addison need a sewer inspection?
faqs.a: No. The village says condos do not schedule the water and sewer account or the sewer and sump pump inspection. A permit release is the only requirement.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run an Addison house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: No. Addison prohibits short-term rentals and treats them as a nuisance. Long-term rentals need the annual Residential Rental License and an inspection.

faqs.q: What were the DuPage County property tax installment dates?
faqs.a: The 2025 taxes came due in two parts, on the first of June and the first of September 2026. The DuPage County Treasurer can confirm the dates on the next bill, and check whether a mortgage servicer already pays your taxes before sending money.
